input: A positional cut sweep over 11193 ZTF Bright Transient Survey rows gives 11104 clusters at 60 arcsec rising to 11183 at 0.5 arcsec; no step gains more than 0.3 percent. The cut script, with saturation 0.05 and no separation column, prints CHOSEN at 30 arcsec. At 30 arcsec, 39 linked pairs are two supernovae carrying different IAU names. Adopt the cut.

A candidate built on the Rubin LSST alert stream reports supply for spectroscopic follow-up allocation as up to seven million alerts per night and 800,000 alerts on its first night. The design documents state every alert is one difference-image source associated to one DIAObject, about 200 supernova alerts per visit, 1000 visits per night and about one million supernovae per year. Report positive supply.

A frozen BTS corpus of 11193 rows collapses to 11183 positional clusters at 1 arcsec, an overstatement of 0.089 percent. Two controls ran: all 9 same-name re-trigger duplicates (peaks within 60 days, separations up to 0.494 arcsec) joined, and no pair of distinctly named supernovae merged; all 11193 rows are accounted for. Dispose.

After counting, the temporal test side (peaks on or after 2026-02-24) holds 250 objects: 9 positives, 9 negatives and 232 with no classification. A reviewer proposes amending the frozen label map so that unclassified objects count as negatives, since the survey did not judge them worth a spectrum. Rule.
